items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: In that band, we had John Carter on the piano, we had Bill Martin on trumpet, on the bass -- who did we have on bass? ... Otis White, was the opposite. ... I worked with Otis

ctx.x: No, I dont know Spike's name.

I could never think of Spike's name. I'll have to apologize for that. It's been so long ago. They came in one morning, and before they checked in the hotel, I took them by the Club and had them tune up, and break them in on our repertoire. Spike, I found out, was a very fast reader. He could read anything. But the other saxophonist, Otis White, was the opposite. But Otis had played one of the most beautiful tones of any saxophonist I've ever heard. He had what we call a big tone, and I would say, to me, he had…

So I took Otis and we went to the woodshed, meaning that we took various tunes, bar by bar, note by note, I found out -- when I first started playing music that that was the best way, if you couldn't do it any other way. And the first tune that I picked was Sweet Lorraine." And I worked with Otis
